title: Session-centric SLOs and Rolling Degradation Policy for Multi-tenant Conversational Sessions
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket defines session-aware SLOs and an automated rolling degradation policy for multi-turn conversational workloads. Goal: specify latency envelopes, per-session availability, and error-budget burn scoring that drive progressive rollout gates and tenant-prioritized degradation during overloads or partial capacity loss. The PRD will: 1) define SLOs (p50/p90/p99 for first-token and per-token latency, session response completeness), 2) define per-tenant SLO tiers and hysteresis rules, 3) define automated rollback and fallback gates (model fallback, regional shunt), and 4) enumerate monitoring, alerting, and CI contract tests required for releases.
acceptance_criteria: Define first-byte and end-of-response latency SLOs separately for interactive sessions (first-token p90 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms) and per-token streaming (p90 <= 40ms).
Establish session-availability SLO: 99.95% success rate for session creation and sustain for P0 tenants, 99.9% for P1, and 99.5% for P2.
Define error-budget model: 30-day rolling window with tenant-weighted burn where high-value tenants consume budgets at double weight.

Specify rolling-degradation plan: when burn-rate > 3x sustained for 30m, apply tiered degradations in order: 1) reduce model size (fallback variant), 2) enable KV-cache aggressive reuse, 3) enable latency-first routing to reserved capacity, 4) soft-throttle non-interactive batch work.
Define hysteresis: once a tenant is degraded, require 60m sustained improvement before auto-restore to avoid flapping.

Define automated rollout gates: unit and integration contract tests passing, end-to-end SLO simulation with synthetic traffic under 2x expected peak, monitoring dashboards and alerting configured, and on-call runbook approved.
Create a rollback playbook with clear thresholds (p99 > 2x SLO for 10m or error-rate spike > 5% absolute) that triggers immediate halt of rollout and escalation.
Include tenant communication templates (email and console banner) for scheduled degradations and SLA impact statements.
notes: Session-aware SLOs require new trace dimensions (session_id, session_length_bucket) in the metrics pipeline.
We should consult Dedicated infra team about reserving burst lanes for P0 tenants during degradations.
Consider coupling rollback gates with model-fidelity regression checks from Redwood Optimize to avoid accuracy regressions after model fallback.
Edge-case: long-running sessions (>10k tokens) may skew per-token p99; propose a separate 'long-session' cohort in SLO reporting.
